# LingoFuse-pasAgent v3

> LingoFuse-pasAgent v3 is an industrial-grade Pascal AI agent toolchain that enables AI clients (Claude, LM Studio, Doubao, DeepSeek, etc.) to directly call Pascal functions as native tools — either via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or via a server-managed tool execution loop. v3 is a **parallel branch of v2** built around **multimodal (text + image) capabilities**, a **four-core-component narrative**, and a **dual-language (Pascal + Python) code generator**. The core generation pipeline is fully deterministic: your Pascal / C declarations are parsed into structured JSON, normalized through a 5-layer transparent pipeline, and generated into MCP tool definitions — no LLM randomness, reproducible results, zero debugging cost.
>
> LingoFuse-pasAgent v3 是工业级 Pascal 智能体技术体系，让 AI 客户端（Claude / LM Studio / 豆包 / DeepSeek 等）直接调用你的 Pascal 函数——既可以走 MCP 协议，也可以走服务端代管工具执行循环。v3 是 **v2 的平行分支**，围绕**多模态（文字 + 图片）**、**四大核心应用组件叙事**、**双语言（Pascal + Python）代码生成器**构建。核心生成链路完全确定性——不依赖 LLM 随机性，结果可复现，零调试成本。

---

## Key facts

- **Repository (v3)**: https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse-pasAgent-v3
- **Repository (v2, still maintained)**: https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse-pasAgent
- **License**: MIT
- **Status**: Active development (v3 project started 2026)
- **Latest doc revision**: 2026-09-17
- **Relationship to v2**: **Parallel branch** — v2 still works and is still maintained; v3 targets multimodal collaboration scenarios
- **Why a new repo**: Multimodal is a *derivative mechanism* requiring coordinated changes across `llm_service` / `llm_proxy` / `llm_proxy_tool` / `llm_client`. Independent repo avoids destabilizing v2.
- **Core mechanism**: MCP (Model Context Protocol) + Pascal + LingoFuse RPC + Multimodal attachments
- **Pre-built package (v3)**: https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse-pasAgent-v3/releases/tag/pre_build
- **Quick start time**: ~10 minutes with pre-built package
- **Runtime dependency**: Visual Studio 2022 VC++ Redistributable (x86/x64)
- **Supported AI clients**: Doubao, LM Studio, Claude, Continue.dev, Jan, DeepSeek, any MCP-compatible client
- **Fully offline capable**: all components run locally
- **Works with any Pascal function**: database, file, hardware, GUI
- **Recommended model (v3)**: `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-UD-IQ4_XS.gguf` (~19.7 GB, **multimodal Omni**, MoE 30B-A3B, ~20 tokens/s on CPU) + **mmproj-F16** vision encoder
- **Legacy model (v2)**: `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-UD-IQ4_NL.gguf` (text-only, kept for reference)
- **Backend compatibility**: 250+ OpenAI-compatible backends (up from 129+ in v2)
- **Related project**: LingoFuse — https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse
- **Related project**: zIPC — https://github.com/PassByYou888/zIPC

---

## v3 vs v2: What changed

| Dimension | v2 | v3 |
|---|---|---|
| **Core narrative** | Three service backends (`llm_service` / `llm_proxy` / `llm_proxy_tool`) | **Four core application components** + one auxiliary tool |
| **`llm_service` role** | One of the three core backends | **Auxiliary verification tool** (embeddable local LLM) |
| **Multimodal** | ❌ Not supported | ✅ **Architecture-level capability** |
| **Recommended model** | Text-only `...-UD-IQ4_NL.gguf` | **Omni multimodal** `...-UD-IQ4_XS.gguf` + mmproj |
| **Code generator** | Pascal output only | **Dual-language output (Pascal + Python)** |
| **Backend compatibility** | 129+ backends | **250+ backends** |
| **Repository** | `LingoFuse-pasAgent` | **`LingoFuse-pasAgent-v3`** (independent) |

---

## Four core application components (+ 1 auxiliary tool)

### 🌟 Tier 1 — Application layer (4 components)

| # | Component | Role | Target scenario |
|:-:|-----------|------|-----------------|
| 1 | **`mcp_api_tool`** | **MCP protocol gateway** (Path A) | Clients with native MCP support (LM Studio / Claude Desktop / Continue.dev) |
| 2 | **`llm_proxy_tool`** (LTB) | **LLM Tool Bridge** (Path B) | Clients without MCP; server-side tool execution; **zero client changes** |
| 3 | **`llm_proxy`** | **Pure text forwarding proxy** | Conversation only, no tools needed |
| 4 | **`llm_client`** | **Pascal client SDK** | Custom Pascal clients that need direct protocol control |

### 🛠️ Tier 2 — Auxiliary verification tool (1 component)

| # | Component | Role | Target scenario |
|:-:|-----------|------|-----------------|
| 5 | **`llm_service`** | **Local inference service** | Air-gapped environments / model verification / **embeddable as your own local LLM tool** |

### 🎨 Development tools (cross-component infrastructure)

| Tool | Role | Why it matters |
|------|------|----------------|
| **`code_decl_to_mcp`** | **Code generator** | ⭐ **One declaration → both Pascal and Python tool providers** |
| **`pascal_agent_service`** | Beacon (tool registry) | Common infrastructure for all tools / gateways |
| **`pascal_agent_api`** | Tool provider example | Your project prototype |
| **`mcp_api_proxy`** | MCP stdio debug proxy | Debug MCP handshakes |
| **`bridge`** | HTTP bridge gateway | Let browsers / Node / PHP access the mesh |
| **`llm_test`** | Command-line REPL test client | Debug LLM services |
| **`HealthCheck`** | Environment health check | First-time deployment validation |

---

## v3's two unique advantages

### 🌐 Advantage 1: Multimodal collaboration — text Q&A + image Q&A

**Other toolchains**: text-only interfaces; cannot understand images.

**pasAgent v3**:
- **Same server, same session**: text Q&A and image Q&A can be mixed
- **Multimodal content construction**: client requests can carry **mixed content** (text + images)
- **Capability declared per modality**: clients can query which modalities the server supports
- **Multi-model backend**: text model + vision encoder (mmproj) working together

### ⭐ Advantage 2: Dual-language code generation — Pascal + Python

**Other toolchains**: require manual callbacks, JSON read/write, tool registration — or support only one language.

**pasAgent v3**:
- **One declaration, two outputs**: Pascal declaration → Pascal tool provider + Python tool provider
- **Zero boilerplate**: `cdecl` callbacks, JSON serialization, tool registration all auto-generated
- **5-layer transparent pipeline**: each layer's JSON is viewable, editable, roll-back-able
- **Deterministic**: main pipeline does not depend on an LLM; reproducible, auditable

---

## Core capabilities

- Exposes Pascal functions as AI-callable tools via MCP protocol
- **Multimodal**: text + image inputs, via `mmproj-F16` / `mmproj-F32` vision encoders
- **Server-side tool execution (Path B)**: clients that only know `generate` get full tool capability
- No MCP protocol knowledge required — write Pascal, AI calls it
- No JSON Schema writing required
- No HTTP service setup required
- **Dual-language code generation**: one declaration → Pascal + Python tool providers
- 5-layer transparent code generation pipeline (source → declaration → JSON → model → tool unit)
- Each layer is independently viewable, editable, exportable, and LLM-assistable
- Main pipeline is fully deterministic — reproducible results, no LLM randomness
- Pre-built DLLs available — download, extract, run
- Supports all MCP clients: Doubao, LM Studio, Claude, Continue.dev, Jan, DeepSeek
- Fully offline: local LLM streaming service included
- UI-compatible: code generator reserves main-thread sync interface
- **Two tool execution paths**:
  - **Path A (client-side)**: For MCP-capable clients. Tools exposed via `mcp_api_tool.exe`.
  - **Path B (server-side)**: For clients that only send `generate`. Tools executed by `llm_proxy_tool.exe` (LTB) — **zero client changes**.
- **Three sibling LLM backends** (only one may run at a time on the default endpoint):
  - `llm_service.exe` — local inference (llama.cpp / GGUF, **multimodal via mmproj**)
  - `llm_proxy.exe` — stateless text proxy to 250+ OpenAI-compatible backends
  - `llm_proxy_tool.exe` (LTB) — proxy + server-side MCP tool execution + multimodal forwarding
- **API capability discovery**: `get_api_capabilities` lets clients learn at runtime what the server supports
- **250+ backend compatibility**: cloud APIs, local servers, gateways, desktop clients, Web UIs, agent frameworks, RAG platforms

---

## How it works

### Path A — client-side tool execution (classic MCP)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U["👤 用户"] --> C["🤖 AI 客户端（支持 MCP）"]
    C -->|MCP| M["🌉 mcp_api_tool.exe"]
    M -->|LF_Call| B["📡 信标<br/>pascal_agent_service.exe"]
    B -->|路由| T["🎯 Pascal 工具<br/>pascal_agent_api.exe"]
    T -.->|结果| B -.-> M -.-> C -.-> U
```

### Path B — server-side tool execution (LTB)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U["👤 用户"] --> C["🤖 AI 客户端（不感知工具）"]
    C -->|LF generate| L["🔴 llm_proxy_tool.exe<br/>LTB"]
    L -->|HTTP SSE + tools| R["🔌 后端<br/>LM Studio / DeepSeek"]
    R -.->|tool_calls| L
    L -->|LF_Call| B["📡 信标"]
    B -->|路由| T["🎯 Pascal 工具"]
    T -.->|结果| B -.-> L
    L -->|role=tool 回填| R
    R -.->|最终文本| L
    L -.->|chunk/think/finish| C --> U
```

### Multimodal (v3 new)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["🖼️ 图片文件"] --> B["🔢 视觉编码器<br/>mmproj-F16 / F32"]
    B --> C["🎫 视觉 token"]
    D["📝 文字提问"] --> E["🔤 文本 tokenizer"]
    E --> F["🎫 文本 token"]
    C --> G["🔗 拼接"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["🧠 Omni GGUF<br/>LLM 主干推理"]
    H --> I["📤 文字回答"]
```

Your Pascal functions → translated by `mcp_api_tool` (Path A) or executed by `llm_proxy_tool` (Path B) → AI client sees standard tools → calls actually execute your Pascal code.

---

## 5-layer transparent code generation pipeline (dual-language output)

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    L0["Layer 0 — 原始 Pascal / C 源码"] --> L1["Layer 1 — 统一声明体"]
    L1 <-.->|双向| L2["Layer 2 — LV0 声明 JSON"]
    L2 --> L3["Layer 3 — LV1 模型 JSON"]
    L3 --> L4P["Layer 4-PAS — 工具提供者单元 .pas"]
    L3 --> L4Py["Layer 4-PY — 工具提供者模块 .py"]
```

| Layer | Content | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 0 | Raw Pascal / C source | Your original code |
| Layer 1 | Unified declaration body | Extracted function signatures |
| Layer 2 | LV0 declaration JSON | Structured declarations |
| Layer 3 | LV1 model JSON | Normalized model |
| Layer 4-PAS | Tool provider unit (.pas) | Generated MCP tool definitions (Pascal) |
| Layer 4-PY | Tool provider module (.py) | Generated MCP tool definitions (Python) |

Each layer can be independently viewed, edited, exported, fed to LLM for assistance, or rolled back on error. The generator itself (`code_decl_to_mcp.exe`) is a **GUI application**, not a command-line tool. Its source lives in the **LingoFuse core repository**, not in this repo.

> ⭐ **Layer 3 is the fork point** — the same LV1 model feeds two generators, producing two target languages. Complexity drops from O(N×M) to O(N+M) as new input/output languages are added.

---

## Component architecture

| Component | Binary / File | Purpose | Target user |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pascal Beacon | `pascal_agent_service.exe` | Register & discover tools across the mesh | Service deployers |
| Pascal Tool Provider | `pascal_agent_api.exe` | Expose your Pascal functions as tools | Pascal developers |
| MCP Gateway (Path A) | `mcp_api_tool.exe` | Translate tools into MCP protocol | MCP-capable clients |
| MCP Debug Proxy | `mcp_api_proxy.exe` | stdio passthrough with JSON-RPC line filtering | Debuggers |
| Code Generator | `code_decl_to_mcp.exe` | Generate tool provider unit from Pascal / C declarations (**dual-language output**) | Developers during development |
| Local LLM Service | `llm_service.exe` | Run local GGUF models (fully offline, **supports multimodal via mmproj**) | Air-gapped users |
| LLM Text Proxy | `llm_proxy.exe` | Forward to **250+** OpenAI-compatible backends | Cloud / LAN users |
| LLM Tool Bridge (LTB) | `llm_proxy_tool.exe` | Proxy + **server-side MCP tool execution** + multimodal forwarding | Clients without MCP |
| LLM Test Client | `llm_test.exe` | Interactive multi-session REPL | Debugging |
| HTTP Bridge | `bridge.exe` | HTTP-to-LingoFuse passthrough | Web ecosystem |
| Health Check | `HealthCheck.exe` | Verify runtime & DLLs | First-time deployers |

**Files you need to care about first**:
- `src/pascal_agent_api.lpr` — arithmetic tool example, your project prototype
- `src/pascal_agent_service.lpr` — the beacon source
- `src/lingofuse_helper.pas` — helper functions for writing tools
- `src/lingofuse/` — LingoFuse Python binding package (packed into EXEs)
- `src/llm_common/` — shared LLM modules (attachments, capabilities, SSE client)

> **Note**: `code_decl_to_mcp` source is **not** in this repository. Only its user manual (`code_generate_mcp.md`) and declaration specs are provided here.

## Quick start (3 steps)

### Step 1: Write a Pascal function

```pascal
function Add(a, b: Integer): Integer;
begin
  Result := a + b;
end;
```

### Step 2: Generate the tool provider unit (GUI)

Launch `code_decl_to_mcp.exe`, paste the declaration, walk through the 5 tabs (source → LV0 JSON → LV1 JSON → final source), then copy the generated file:

- **Pascal side** (`pas_TabSheet`) → save as `.pas` → `lazbuild` to compile
- **Python side** (`Py_TabSheet`) → save as `.py` → **run directly with `python`**

### Step 3: Compile and start

```bash
# Compile the generated tool unit (use lazbuild, NOT raw fpc)
lazbuild -B ./your_tools.lpi

# Start the beacon (must run first)
pascal_agent_service.exe

# Start the tool provider (registers itself to the beacon)
your_tools.exe

# Start the MCP gateway (Path A)
mcp_api_tool.exe
```

AI can now call your Pascal function. For the complete step-by-step guide, see `Pascal_Integration_Guide.md`.

### Path B — client does not support MCP

```bash
# Start LTB instead of mcp_api_tool
llm_proxy_tool.exe --backend-url http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 --mcp-reg-agent-app llm_proxy_agent
```

Your client only sends `generate`. LTB handles the entire tool-call loop internally.

### Multimodal (v3 new)

```bash
# Local multimodal inference: Omni model + mmproj vision encoder
llm_service.exe `
  --model-path .\NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-UD-IQ4_XS.gguf `
  --mmproj .\mmproj-F16.gguf

# Or forward to a vision-capable backend
llm_proxy_tool.exe --backend-url http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 --backend-model "qwen2-vl-7b-instruct" --vision
```

### Pre-built package (no environment setup)

1. Download [Pre-built Package (v3)](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse-pasAgent-v3/releases/tag/pre_build)
2. Extract to e.g. `C:\Temp\temp2`
3. Follow `Pascal_Integration_Guide.md`
4. Call your first Pascal tool from AI in 10 minutes

### Clone

```bash
git clone --recursive https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse-pasAgent-v3.git
# If already cloned without --recursive:
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

---

## Recommended model (v3): Omni multimodal

**`NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-UD-IQ4_XS.gguf`** + **mmproj-F16** vision encoder

- **Type**: Multimodal (Omni) — text + image
- **Architecture**: MoE — Mamba-2 + MoE + Attention hybrid, 30B total / ~3B active per token
- **Context**: up to 1M tokens (256K native default)
- **CPU speed**: ~20 tokens/s (thanks to 3B active parameters)
- **Cost**: **lowest energy per task** among compared candidates (Qwen3.6 / Qwen3.8 / Meta series)
- **Vision**: requires `mmproj-F16` (recommended) or `mmproj-F32` (higher precision)
- **Quantization architectures available**: `Q4_K_M`, `UD-Q4_K_XL`, `IQ4_NL`, `IQ4_XS`, `Q5_K_M`, `Q8_0`, etc. — **download several, benchmark on your own hardware**
- **Speech**: ❌ **not supported** — Chinese Mandarin + dialects are extremely hard to reconcile; TTS licensing / ownership restrictions block clean open-source options. Will be reconsidered in the future.

Full download & deployment guide: `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-UD-IQ4_XS.md`

## API capability discovery

Every LingoFuse LLM service publishes a capability matrix through the `get_api_capabilities` Call API, so that clients can short-circuit unsupported operations locally.

| API | `llm_service` | `llm_proxy` | `llm_proxy_tool` (LTB) |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `generate` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `create_session` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `close_session` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `cancel_session` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `list_sessions` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| **`set_system_message`** | **1** | **0** | **0** |
| `health` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `llm_stream` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| **`tools`** / **`tool_calls`** / **`tool_results`** | — | — | **1** |
| `server_kind` | `service` | `proxy` | `proxy` |

> **Note**: `llm_proxy` and `llm_proxy_tool` both report `server_kind = "proxy"`. To distinguish them, read the LTB-specific `tools` / `tool_calls` fields.

---

## Streaming protocol

All services push structured JSON via the `llm_stream` Notify API:

| Type | Fields | Meaning |
|------|--------|---------|
| `chunk` | `session_id`, `text` | Body stream |
| `think` | `session_id`, `text` | Reasoning stream (reasoning models only) |
| `finish` | `session_id`, `reason` | Generation finished |
| `error` | `session_id`, `message` | Server error |
| `closed` | `session_id`, `reason` | Session closed |

Clients only read the `type` field. No "magic strings".

---

## Coexistence rules

| Combination | Can run simultaneously? | Notes |
|---|:---:|---|
| `llm_proxy_tool` + `mcp_api_tool` | ✅ **Yes** | Different `reg_agent` names (`llm_proxy_agent` vs `reg_agent`), shared beacon |
| `llm_proxy_tool` + `llm_proxy` | ❌ No | Share the default `ipc:llm_service` endpoint |
| `llm_proxy_tool` + `llm_service` | ❌ No | Share the default `ipc:llm_service` endpoint |
| `llm_proxy_tool` + `llm_service` (different endpoints) | ✅ Yes | Give LTB `--endpoint ipc:llm_proxy_tool --app-name LLM_Proxy_Tool` |

---

## FAQ

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Do I need to know MCP protocol? | **No** — just write Pascal |
| Does it only support Doubao? | **No** — supports all MCP clients: Doubao / LM Studio / Claude / Continue.dev / Jan / DeepSeek |
| Can it only do arithmetic? | **Any Pascal function** — database, file, hardware, GUI |
| **What is v3 vs v2?** | v3 is a **parallel branch** of v2 — v2 still works, v3 targets **multimodal collaboration** |
| **Why is v3 a separate repo?** | Multimodal is a *derivative mechanism* requiring coordinated changes; independent repo avoids destabilizing v2 |
| **What is multimodal?** | Letting AI process **both text and images** as input, not just text |
| Does it need internet? | **No** — all components run locally (unless using `llm_proxy` / `llm_proxy_tool` with a cloud backend) |
| Can my function operate UI? | **Yes** — generated code reserves main-thread sync interface |
| Missing DLL and don't want to compile? | **Download the pre-built package** — extract and run |
| What if my client doesn't support MCP? | **Use `llm_proxy_tool.exe` (Path B)** — the server handles the tool loop |
| Can the three LLM backends run simultaneously? | **No (by default)** — they share `ipc:llm_service`. Override `--endpoint` + `--app-name` to coexist |
| **Which model is recommended in v3?** | **`NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-UD-IQ4_XS.gguf` + mmproj-F16** (~20 t/s on CPU, 1M context, multimodal) |
| **Why this model and not Qwen3.6 / 3.8 / Meta?** | Best **composite** across **multimodal + performance + energy cost** — lowest energy per task among compared candidates |
| **Do I need to download only one quantization?** | **No** — download several (`Q4_K_M`, `UD-Q4_K_XL`, `IQ4_XS`, etc.) and benchmark on your hardware. Offload / performance / compatibility vary per architecture |
| **Does it support speech?** | ❌ **Not yet** — Mandarin + dialect reconciliation is complex; TTS licensing / ownership restrictions block clean open-source options. Future work planned |
| What does the code generator output? | **Both Pascal and Python tool providers** — see `code_generate_mcp.md` |
| Where is the code generator source? | **In the LingoFuse core repository** — this repo only ships the user manual |
| Is there a Python client? | **No** — Python can already reach the agent ecosystem natively (LangChain / OpenAI SDK / …); no need to route through LingoFuse |

---

## Relation to LingoFuse

pasAgent v3 is a branch project of LingoFuse. LingoFuse provides the cross-language RPC mesh and service discovery infrastructure. pasAgent builds on top of it to expose Pascal functions as MCP tools for AI agents. Both are fully open, non-commercial, community-driven projects under MIT license.

**v3 vs v2 relationship**: v3 is a **parallel branch**, not a replacement. v2 remains available and maintained; v3 targets **multimodal collaboration** scenarios.
